replication.target_description: Study 1, section 4.4: Pearson correlation of all PythonTA errors remaining in a final graded Python submission with percentage of correctness tests failed. This is the conceptual replication of the overall-grades/all-static-analysis-errors relationship, explicitly contrasted with the original in the same paragraph.

n.sample_role: Final graded submissions (observations), not unique participants; target-test analytic count not explicitly printed.
n.exclusions: Target-correlation exclusions not reported. Methods retain consented students and omit repeat-enrolled students from the Summer 2023 dataset.

reported_success.location: p. 83, section 4.4; p. 84, section 5.1; p. 85, sections 5.3 and 7
reported_success.quote: The original Edwards et al. study did not find a clear correlation ... (𝑅 = −0.27) between overall grades and all static analysis errors. ... Our findings are generally consistent with the Edwards et al. study, ... though with some notable differences.

notes: Only assigned unfinished fields were evaluated; original is an unassigned placeholder. Same-test p < .001 retained with the printed R = −0.53. Preserve the printed negative sign despite the text describing percentage of correctness tests failed. The separate Coding Flaws correlation R = −0.54 is not this target. Table 1 prints 1270 participants, 34629 interim submissions, and 15060 final submissions; these are corpus counts, with no explicit N attached to the critical Pearson test. Section 4.4 continues on p. 84 with G1/G2/G3 counts 2086, 726, 641 for a distinct grouped coding-flaw correctness analysis; these were not summed or transferred to the all-errors correlation. No N derived from df. Authors provide a general paper-level verdict (Our findings are generally consistent with the Edwards et al. study, ... though with some notable differences.), but no explicit success/failure verdict for the assigned all-errors correlation; significance alone was not converted into replication success.
